why: Search by the ordering, remembering the last place you turned left: the successor is either the leftmost node of the target's right subtree or, if there is none, the lowest ancestor whose left subtree holds the target.
hints: The successor is the smallest value larger than the target. Where can such a value live relative to the target?
Walk from the root: when node.val > target, it is a candidate; record it and go left. When node.val <= target, go right. The last candidate recorded is the answer.
One loop down the tree, O(h) time, O(1) space. Return -1 if no candidate was recorded.
pitfalls: The successor can be an ancestor, not only a node in the right subtree.
The largest value has no successor: return -1.
